title: The Cipher of Geneva Again
premise: Elodie Sterling, a disgraced intelligence analyst living under a polished false identity in Geneva, notices that a transatlantic flight has been erased from every database while still airborne—a signature only one dead adversary ever used. Pulled back into the orbit of the three agencies that discarded them, Elodie assembles a makeshift team of fellow castoffs: a retired air-traffic controller, a forger, and the one person who remembers who Elodie used to be. Together they uncover a plot to stage a midair catastrophe over Frankfurt timed to trigger an algorithmic market collapse, disguised as pilot error. In the end, Elodie must broadcast the truth from inside the erased flight's ghost record, sacrificing their anonymity forever but gaining, for the first time, a family that knows their real name.
about_author: Wren Kavanagh is the pen name of a former aviation-industry consultant who spent a decade writing risk assessments no one read. They live near Lake Geneva with two rescue dogs and an unhealthy knowledge of flight-tracking software.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Elodie Sterling's POV. A quiet morning in Geneva: coffee, a rehearsed cover story, a packed bag they never unpack. We learn how three agencies burned them and why invisibility feels like safety. Emotional beat: brittle calm masking hypervigilance.

chapters.title: Flight 4471 Does Not Exist
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Scrolling flight data out of habit, Elodie watches a live aircraft blink out of every tracker, registry, and booking system—while its transponder still pings overhead. Emotional beat: the thrill of recognition curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Old Numbers, New Voices
chapters.summary: Elodie calls a contact from their second agency life; the line is answered by someone using Elodie's own old codename. First hint that someone is resurrecting a buried operation. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: The Controller Who Retired Twice
chapters.summary: Marek Ostrowski's POV. A former air-traffic controller in Zurich recognizes the vanished flight's altitude profile as impossible and starts his own quiet inquiry. He and Elodie meet awkwardly, two ghosts comparing notes. Emotional beat: wary kinship.

chapters.title: What the Forger Charges
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. To access sealed records, Elodie hires Ines Baptiste, a document forger who once faked Elodie's first identity. Ines agrees—for a price Elodie can't pay in money. Emotional beat: transactional trust with real warmth underneath.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, One Denial
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie approaches their old handlers; each agency denies the flight existed and each offers, too quickly, to 'take care of' Elodie's curiosity. Someone senior is frightened. Emotional beat: humiliation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Person Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Sofia Reyes's POV. Sofia, Elodie's former partner and the only keeper of their true name, is living in Lyon under her own lies. She receives a coded postcard she hasn't seen since training. Emotional beat: longing tangled with anger.

chapters.title: Ghost Manifest
chapters.summary: Elodie and Marek reconstruct the erased passenger list from boarding-gate CCTV and credit-card traces. One name recurs across three other 'accidents': a shell company called Meridian Lattice. Emotional beat: pattern-recognition euphoria turning to horror.

chapters.title: Ines's Price
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Ines reveals her fee: Elodie's original identity file, so she can study the master forger who trained them both—and who betrayed them. Emotional beat: reluctant honesty as currency.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens at Nine
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Cross-referencing flight paths with derivatives markets, Marek finds the crash corridor is calibrated to a single trading window Monday morning. The 'accident' is a financial weapon. Emotional beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: Sofia Lands
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Sofia arrives uninvited at Elodie's flat, holding the postcard and a gun she doesn't draw. Their history detonates quietly: what Elodie did to survive the third agency. Emotional beat: rupture before repair.

chapters.title: The Training House Burns Again
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Elodie's POV. Years earlier: the betrayal at the facility where Elodie, Ines, and their mentor were made and unmade. We finally see what 'burnt analyst' means. Emotional beat: grief given context.

chapters.title: Meridian Lattice Has a Face
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Following the forgery signatures, Ines identifies the architect: Anton Veyra, their presumed-dead mentor, alive and selling engineered catastrophes. Emotional beat: betrayal layered on betrayal.

chapters.title: Surveillance Is a Love Language
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. The four misfits set up in a safehouse above a laundromat, bickering over tradecraft, sharing bad takeout, building something like a family. Emotional beat: found-family warmth amid rising stakes.

chapters.title: The Second Erasure
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Veyra erases Elodie next—bank accounts, lease, identity—leaving them legally nonexistent hours before the attack. Staying invisible was never an option; now it isn't even possible. Emotional beat: liberation through loss.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes Over the Rhine
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek infiltrates the regional control center and confirms the target flight: a Frankfurt-bound commuter deliberately loaded with Meridian-linked executives meant to die 'pilot error.' Emotional beat: ticking-clock urgency.

chapters.title: What Sofia Carried
chapters.summary: Sofia's POV. Sofia confesses she was sent by the second agency to retrieve or silence Elodie—and chose instead to warn them. Trust is rebuilt on truth rather than loyalty. Emotional beat: forgiveness earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Broadcasting a Ghost
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The plan: reinsert Flight 4471's erased record into Eurocontrol's live feed with evidence of tampering attached, forcing human controllers to ground the aircraft. Ines forges the credentials; Marek works the frequencies. Emotional beat: desperate competence.

chapters.title: Veyra's Cockpit
chapters.summary: Climax part one, alternating POVs. Veyra, aboard as a passenger, triggers the final override; Elodie confronts him via the aircraft's datalink, using shared memories as proof of identity. Emotional beat: duel between maker and made.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Climax part two, ensemble POV rotation. The ghost flight blinks back into existence on every screen at once; controllers scramble the jet to an emergency landing as markets wobble and hold. Veyra is taken—but the system that enabled him isn't. Emotional beat: exhale without triumph.

chapters.title: Testimony Under a Real Name
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie testifies to three parliamentary committees as Elodie Sterling, no alias, watching agencies flinch. Anonymity is gone; so is the lie. Emotional beat: terrifying freedom.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Elodie's POV. Weeks later: the go-bag sits empty in a closet, replaced by a spare toothbrush for Sofia, Marek's chess set, Ines's sketchbooks. Elodie finally unpacks. Emotional beat: home as a choice, not a cover.
